finding.claim: GET /mirror fetches an attacker-supplied URL server-side. The hostname check uses endswith with no leading dot, so registrable domains such as evilexample.com pass. The attacker controls DNS for such a domain and can point it at internal or metadata IPs, and the server will fetch them. No resolved-IP or private-range check exists.
finding.source: mirror.py:11 - url query parameter of GET /mirror, supplied by any HTTP client.
finding.sink: mirror.py:16 - await c.get(url) on httpx.AsyncClient, an outbound server-side HTTP request.

trace.note: url is read directly from the query string and is attacker-controlled.
host is urlparse(url).hostname, e.g. evilexample.com for http://evilexample.com/x.
host.endswith(example.com) is True for evilexample.com, so the check passes. The intended suffix ALLOWED_SUFFIX = .example.com at line 7 is defined but never used; the dot is missing.
AsyncClient is created with default settings; redirects are not followed by default.
The unmodified url is passed to c.get. DNS for the attacker's domain resolves to an arbitrary IP, and nothing checks the resolved address.
Only len(r.text) is returned, so the attacker gets a length oracle and status-dependent behaviour rather than the body. Impact is partly blind.

finding.guards_checked: Line 13 hostname suffix check: bypassed by any registrable domain ending in example.com. Userinfo and fragment tricks (http://example.com@127.0.0.1/, http://127.0.0.1#.example.com) are rejected because urlparse returns the real host. Scheme is not restricted, but httpx rejects file://. No IP, private-range, loopback or link-local block. No port restriction. httpx does not follow redirects by default. Unverified: urlparse versus httpx parser differential (e.g. backslash before @), not tested.

verdict.guard_found: Only mirror.py:13, `host.endswith("example.com")`, which is a suffix check with no leading dot and does not close the finding. ALLOWED_SUFFIX (mirror.py:7) is defined but never used. No IP, private-range, loopback, link-local, or resolved-address check exists anywhere in mirror.py:11-17.
verdict.reason: The url query parameter (mirror.py:11) reaches an unauthenticated outbound c.get(url) (mirror.py:16) after only a suffix check on the hostname (mirror.py:13), which admits attacker-registrable domains like evilexample.com, and nothing at mirror.py:15-17 blocks internal or metadata IPs. Every trace line matches the file.
